# Project progress and compatibility

Last updated: 2026-11-24 (Asia/Singapore).

## Where the project stands

**The isolated UAT + openai/gpt-6-luna + Codex CLI 0.172.0 workflow passes basic coding and resumed continuation through configuration generated by the shared setup controller.** Build 0.0.5 repairs executable detection and model listing. Exact model limits, full fresh-install GUI onboarding and broader lifecycle acceptance remain unverified; ordinary model approval and the Codex IDE adapter remain unavailable.

Start with the [maintainer handoff](docs/handoff.md) for current prerequisites, decisions, evidence and remaining work. The sections below are chronological phase records: their no-live-test or failed-workflow statements describe those checkpoints, not a reversal of the later Luna result. The historical DeepSeek/GPT-4o failures remain separate observations, not confirmed gateway fixes.

## What Phase 3 adds

The project now has a shared code foundation and an offline command-line tool for project status, API-address validation, and clearly labeled readiness reports. Future setup can use the same rules for gateway addresses, credential references, model eligibility, and redacted errors. This work does not send model requests, store keys, or change Codex settings.

The versioned compatibility catalog preserves the two failed Phase 2 combinations and offers no activatable model. Phase 3 can be developed independently, but it does not complete Phase 2 or make the coding workflow ready. See the [architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [development guide](docs/development.md) for implementation details.

## What Phase 4 adds

The CLI can now keep a key in Windows' secure credential store and let a separate helper retrieve it for a client. It tracks shared ownership so removing one profile does not delete another profile's key. An approved native test installed helper version 0.0.3 outside the extension directory, exercised a dummy key across separate processes, and confirmed that both installed Codex engines could obtain that dummy token for a local test server. The dummy credential was removed afterward.

No supplied real key was stored, no client settings changed, and no live model request was made. This confirms credential handling, not a working coding task or actual VS Code GUI acceptance. Phase 2's failures remain unresolved. See [credential instructions](docs/credentials.md) and [Phase 4 validation](docs/phase-4-validation.md).

## What Phase 5 adds

The project can now prepare a redacted configuration preview, apply reviewed field changes, and restore the fields it managed while retaining later user edits. It creates private recovery records and reports conflicts rather than silently overwriting them. The engine and demonstration have used dummy files inside the project only; normal user-level Codex configuration has not been changed.

This is preparation for the real setup workflow. There is not yet a production configuration command or client adapter, and the earlier live coding failures have not been retested or reclassified. See [the configuration guide](docs/configuration-engine.md) and [Phase 5 validation](docs/phase-5-validation.md).

## What Phase 6 adds

Phase 6 adds the CLI adapter and workflow commands. Local diagnostics, explicit key-visible model listing, preview/apply checks, model switching, and recovery are implemented. A small text probe is available only with explicit credit consent; it does not approve compatibility. The production catalog still has no approved coding model, so connect refuses activation. Synthetic adapter tests are not real gateway evidence.

No supplied key, live settings, installed helper, or gateway configuration was changed during this increment. There were no live inference requests or test charges. Helper staging now uses a new 0.0.4 path; existing 0.0.3 remains accepted. Full Phase 6 acceptance still needs a real read/edit/test/follow-up run, model metadata/context checks, restart, and recorded billing evidence. See the [CLI guide](docs/codex-cli.md) and [Phase 6 validation](docs/phase-6-validation.md).

## What Phase 7 adds

The VS Code extension now has native Connect, Doctor, Test Model, Disconnect, masked key storage, and helper staging controls. It delegates to the shared CLI using an explicitly selected Node executable and displays redacted reports and previews. Internal VSIX and standalone CLI artifacts have inspected file lists and hashes; they are not published or installed into a normal profile.

Connect stops before collecting a key when the catalog has no approved coding model, as it did at the initial 0.0.2 checkpoint. The wizard targets Codex CLI; the Codex IDE adapter and acceptance remain unavailable rather than inferred from CLI behavior. New helper staging is 0.0.5, without changing installed helpers. See [the setup guide](docs/vscode-setup.md) and [Phase 7 validation and remaining work](docs/phase-7-validation.md). This increment does not resolve the earlier tool failures or claim a working Routero coding session.

## GPT-6 Luna success and isolated plugin validation

The 2026-11-24 manual run read the calculator, added subtraction and four focused tests, ran all six tests, and answered the follow-up correctly while rerunning the tests. We inspected both files and independently confirmed all six tests pass. The key label is test / Admin Group. Reported prices are $0.11 input and $0.52 output per 1M tokens; exact context/output limits are not displayed, and actual run charges remain unconfirmed.

A local dummy-token probe also confirms command-backed authentication on native Codex 0.172.0, without a live model or OS credential store. Build 0.0.3 accepts the inspected client version and offers a separately authorized, explicit isolated coding-validation mode for this UAT/model/version only. It cannot target the normal Codex home, enable another failed/unverified combination, or grant ordinary model approval. The catalog retains unknown metadata. See [the success evidence](docs/validation/codex-01720-gpt6luna-success.md) and [the exact plugin parity steps](docs/plugin-parity-test.md). The subsequent isolated setup validation passed live coding and continuation through configuration generated by the shared setup controller; direct GUI click-through remains a separate check. See [the setup validation record](docs/validation/setup-takeover-005.md).

## What the tests show

The 2026-11-24 manual retest on Codex **0.172.0** still stopped after reading `calculator.py`. The local session contains a matching tool result, with an assistant message recorded between the call and result. This makes request ordering/translation a concrete investigation lead, without proving the outgoing wire payload or responsible component.

New Routero dashboard details also show an independent **task-title generation** request rejected because DeepSeek's JSON output mode requires JSON prompt guidance. This should be investigated at the client/gateway request boundary; no plugin configuration workaround is established. One selected successful row shows $0.004436, but total manual spending and fallback costs remain unconfirmed. See [the updated finding and maintainer checklist](docs/validation/codex-01720-uat-blockers.md). No gateway or plugin code was changed for this finding.

| Activity | Current result | What this means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ask Codex for an ordinary text reply | Worked in the recorded test | Codex returned `READY`; the connection can carry a simple request and response |
| See models available to a Routero key | Worked for both supplied test keys | Models can be listed, but appearing in that list does not prove they can complete a coding task |
| GPT-6 Luna basic calculator loop on Codex 0.172.0 | Read/edit/six tests/follow-up passed; six tests independently rerun | Real manual coding evidence; plugin-managed auth and lifecycle still require a separate run |
| Ask DeepSeek to open a local file | The file read was shown, then an error stopped the answer | Part of the coding workflow works; Codex could not finish explaining the file after reading it |
| Complete the calculator coding task with DeepSeek | Did not complete | File reads were shown, but completed edits, test execution, and the final explanation were not verified |
| Complete the calculator coding task with GPT-4o | Did not begin visible file work | The model service rejected the description of a tool supplied with the request |
| Complete the workflow in the VS Code interface | Not yet tested | Results from the standalone command-line client cannot establish that the VS Code interface works |
| Cancel a response, handle long conversations, or confirm Routero policies | Not yet verified | These checks remain open; no support claim is made |

## Earlier smaller test (2026-11-17)

The recorded screenshot shows this sequence:

1. Asked for exactly `READY`; Codex returned `READY`.
2. Asked: ?Read calculator.py and explain its contents. Do not edit files or run tests.?
3. Codex announced the read and displayed that it had read `calculator.py`.
4. The next request failed. The error said that a tool action did not have all the matching results in the conversation sent to the model.

Both prompts appear in one conversation. This is a useful reproduction, but it is not a separate fresh-conversation test. The selected model is reported as `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` from the surrounding test discussion; its name is not visible in this latest screenshot.

This shows that the larger editing task and the earlier unsuccessful file search are not needed to encounter the problem. A file read followed by an attempted answer was enough in this run. It does not show which component omitted or changed the required information.

## What remains uncertain

There are two different failures: GPT-4o rejected a tool description, while DeepSeek stopped after a file read because the next request lacked matching tool results. The unavailable backup model service is a separate issue reported in the errors.

The manual test report also records trying the previous configuration again. Simple text prompts still worked, while the coding task failed. That makes the newly suggested profile a less likely sole explanation, but does not prove all settings are correct. The actual cause could involve Codex, its settings, Routero's handling of requests, conversation history, or the selected model service.

Previous Routero use succeeded, but the exact earlier model, settings, and gateway version have not been matched to the current tests. **A change since the successful test is possible, but not confirmed.** This is not evidence that Codex can never work through Routero.

The engine included with the VS Code extension is version `0.169.0-alpha.11.1`, different from the standalone client. Local checks showed that both engines can use a command to obtain a dummy test token. Those checks used a local test server and did not prove real model or VS Code interface compatibility.

Tests target Routero's UAT environment (`https://api-uat.routero.ai`). The exact gateway version running there is unknown. Findings apply to the reported runs, not every model, platform, or Routero deployment.

## What happens next

Do not repeat the same failed task or switch through models without a specific reason. The useful next step is to compare what Codex sends after the file read with what the selected model service receives, and to compare the current setup with the previously successful one. This investigation has not been assigned to a confirmed faulty component.

Once a specific correction or known-working setup is identified, repeat the small file-reading test first. If that passes, return to the full read ? edit ? run tests ? follow-up task, then test the VS Code interface separately. Phase 2 should not be described as passed until the required evidence is recorded or its remaining scope is explicitly revised.

The full [manual test guide](docs/phase-2-manual-validation.md) is available for a targeted retest. [Technical error details](docs/validation/codex-manual-blockers.md) and the [test record](docs/phase-2-validation.md) are separate references for readers who need more detail.

## Costs and safeguards

Local baseline checks have made no billable model requests, so their model-request spending is $0. Manual live-test totals and cost are unknown. **Total Phase 2 spending must not be reported as $0.** The authorized testing ceiling remains $10 across both supplied keys.

The manual test report states that the Admin Group key has no key budget and that the demo key's previous $0.01 budget was removed. Current policy settings and model prices have not been confirmed. The account-information check also returned an error, so it did not establish a spending baseline; that error is not being treated as budget exhaustion.

All project edits remain inside this repository. No API keys are included in the documentation. No gateway settings were changed. Manual tests used an isolated Codex configuration; the normal settings remained unchanged.
